**Risk officer call: REFUSE. No position size.**

The brief doesn't clear the bar on any axis. The class is OPERATOR, which has only been break-even on average, and this coin shows the operator pattern at its most concentrated: 1,992 SOL bought in the first two minutes from 16 wallets, with top-5 buyers holding 99.9% and the bundle share at 1.0. That is a supply structure where one actor can exit at will.

Recent flow is also weak. Last 15 minutes: 11.8 SOL bought against 9.2 SOL sold, net flow +2.65 SOL, and return of 0.25%. Costs of 1.4-5.1% per round trip would consume any edge.

The name ("Global Oil Institution Fund") is an institutional-sounding claim the creator chose. I treat it as noise, not as evidence of backing.

If the desk ever revisited this coin, the minimum conditions would be: a materially dispersed holder base, sellers no longer outnumbering buyers in the window, and a drawdown that has already stabilized. None of those are present. Skip.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying GOIF now is thin. The strongest point is that the coin is alive at 30.8 minutes, with a 2.3% return over 30 minutes, no drawdown from its 30-minute high, a 2,081 SOL pool, and $2.5k of volume in the last 15 minutes. Net flow over that window was positive (+2.65 SOL), with 46 buyers against 30 sellers.

Against that, the brief shows an operator-class coin: one bundle took 100% of the curve, and the top five post-graduation buyers hold 99.9% of early buys (1,992 SOL from 16 wallets in two minutes). The last 15 minutes show a bit more sell pressure (9.17 SOL sold vs 11.81 bought), and the quoted $29M market cap looks inflated relative to a pool of about 2,000 SOL. The name, which evokes institutional credibility, is a creator-chosen label and tells us nothing about real demand.

I can't find a case that real, independent demand will persist for 30 to 60 minutes. The recent-flow signal is modest, and the concentration profile points to a single operator controlling supply. Operator-backed coins have roughly broken even, and the desk's fees of 1.4 to 5.1% eat into any edge. Recommendation: no buy. Skipping costs nothing.
memos.skeptic: The most likely way this loses money is insider distribution by the operator cluster. In the first two minutes after graduation, 1,992 SOL came in from 16 buyers, with top5 buyer share at 0.9994 and a launch bot present. The curve shows bundle_share 1.0 and top3_share 1.0, so essentially the whole supply sits with a bundled group whose cost basis is far below anything a $20 ticket can match. Sell-side activity is already visible: last 15 minutes show 9.17 SOL sold against 11.81 bought, with 30 sellers, and net flow of only +2.65 SOL. The 30-minute return of +2.3% is thin, and the 0.0% drawdown means nothing yet, since a single distribution wave can take a pool this size down far past the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost. The name, "Global Oil Institution Fund," is a creator-chosen label that implies legitimacy, which is data about the pitch, not evidence of backing. Skip.
